topic: Massage before or after a race or big event

slides.headline: Timing your massage around race day
slides.sub: How to plan it so it helps, not hinders.

slides.title: Nothing new in race week
slides.body: Race week isn't the time to try a deep tissue massage for the first time. If massage is already part of your routine, stick with what you know works for your body.

slides.title: Before: go lighter, go earlier
slides.body: If you like a pre-event massage, book it two to four days out and ask for lighter pressure. Deep work close to a race can leave you feeling sore or flat on the day.

slides.title: After: wait a day or two
slides.body: Straight after a big event, rest, rehydrate, eat and walk it out. A gentle massage a day or two later can help you feel less stiff. Save deeper work for later in the week.

slides.title: Set realistic expectations
slides.body: Research suggests massage can reduce how sore you feel after exercise, but it doesn't replace sleep, food, easy movement or a sensible return to training. Think of it as one helpful piece.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Sharp pain that stops you running, swelling, pain on one specific spot of bone, or calf pain with warmth and swelling need a proper assessment by a physio or GP, not a massage.

slides.headline: Got an event coming up?
slides.body: Book with our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy. Tell us your event date and we'll plan pressure and timing around it.

caption:
Massage before a race or after it? Timing matters more than you'd think.

Race week isn't the time to try deep tissue work for the first time. If you like a pre-event massage, book it two to four days out and keep the pressure lighter. Deep work too close to the start line can leave you feeling flat.

Afterwards, rest, rehydrate, eat and walk it out first. A gentle massage a day or two later can ease stiffness, with deeper work later in the week. Research suggests massage can reduce soreness, but it complements sleep, food and easy movement rather than replacing them.

Sharp pain, swelling or pain on a specific spot of bone needs a proper assessment instead.
